newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's OTP Securities rates Danubius as hold.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's OTP Securities rates Danubius as hold.

text.p: Hungary's OTP Securities said on Thursday it initiated coverage of hotel chain Danubius Hotels Rt as "hold" saying it did not expect much further rise in the shares soon.

"Although we see the future of the company as positive, after the big price jump at the beginning of 1997 we expect a flat price performance in short term," analysts Gabor Korondan and Zoltan Nemeth said in a company report.
At 1053 GMT on the Budapest Stock Exchange Danubius shares traded at 5,200 forints, down 295 forints from Wednesday's close.
The analysts calculated that Danubius' price surged 282 percent in dollar terms in 1996 and in 1997 reached an all-time high of 6,615 forints on February 12 from 4,250 at the end of 1996.
They praised Danubius's acquisition of HungarHotels hotel chain last year, saying it was "the beginning of a new chapter in its history".
"The management at Danubius correctly recognised that profits would stagnate unless a significant acquisition was made," the analysts added.
Danubius itself operates spa hotels and via HungarHotels it acquired city hotels as well.
"The HungarHotels chain already operates profitably and has significant growth potential since its operating figures lag behind those of Danubius," Korondan and Nemeth said.
Danubius, led by a professional management, could benefit from the positive tourism trend in Hungary, they said.

"Optimism is justified by the upward trend in Hungarian tourism, which is ranked seventh in the world for number of tourists," they added. "However, revenues are much less than implied by its ranking."
